findings.text: Provides cached folio lookup by mapping and index with caller selected behaviours for acquiring the folio lock, marking access or clearing idle on write intent, waiting for stable content, creating when missing, allowing nonblocking or filesystem free allocation, and adjusting caching hints. Success returns a referenced folio, absence without creation signals a missing entry, and nonblocking contention is reported as retryable.

Scans present cache entries over a caller supplied index interval, appending referenced results to a batch together with their indices, and advances the caller start cursor past the last collected entry using the entry span rounded to natural alignment. Runs under read side protection and reports how many entries were collected.
Offers a thin wrapper that collects present folios over an index interval into a caller batch by delegating to a tagged variant with the present tag.

Collects a contiguous run of folios starting at a cursor, stopping at interval end, batch capacity, swapped or special values, or a sibling entry indicating landing inside a larger folio. Each candidate is validated with a reference attempt and reload check, the cursor advances across each accepted folio, and start finally moves to the index after the last folio.

Collects folios that are dirty or under writeback over an interval, skipping clean folios and special values, with opportunistic locking to test cleanliness without blocking. Updates the start cursor to resume after the last examined folio or to the interval end, with explicit handling to avoid overflow at the maximum index value.

Provides asynchronous readahead triggered when a marked folio is encountered. Clears the marker, suppresses work when readahead is disabled or the folio is under writeback or the block layer reports congestion, then either extends a sequential window or probes for a recent miss to establish a new window, grows the window geometrically, aligns its end, records async size, and dispatches ordered allocation and submission.

Provides synchronous readahead for a miss at a given index. Handles disabled readahead or congestion with a minimal forced read, honours random access mode with a forced path, recognises sequential arrival at file start or after the previous position, otherwise inspects recent cache history to distinguish isolated random reads from streams, establishes start size and async portion, and dispatches ordered allocation.

Provides ordered readahead allocation over a window. Caps the window at file size, suppresses the future marker when reaching end of file, clamps folio order between mapping limits and window size, iterates with alignment and end of file adjustments, allocates and inserts folios with marker handling, submits the batch, and falls back to classic readahead when large folio support is absent or allocation stops early.

Entry orchestration for buffered read preparation over a byte range. Computes first and beyond end indices from position and count, repeatedly gathers a read batch, issues synchronous readahead when empty, creates and reads a folio when still empty, triggers asynchronous readahead on marked tail folios, ensures the tail is current, handles truncated retry and interrupt on fatal signal, and consumes the tail on failure while preserving earlier batch contents.

Creation aligns the index to mapping minimum order, derives requested order from mapping minimum and caller hint, clamps to mapping maximum, reduces order when misaligned, and retries descending orders with hardened allocation flags for larger orders. Successful insertion stops the loop, concurrent insertion races repeat the lookup, failures propagate with nonblocking exhaustion translated to retryable status, and mmap creation unlocks the newly inserted folio.

Read batch gathering stops at interval end, batch capacity, special values, sibling entries, a folio that is not current, or a folio carrying a readahead marker, after validating references with reload checks. It advances across each accepted folio span and runs under read side protection with reset and retry on transient races.

Range currency treats fully current folios as current, rejects partial currency when the caller requires full currency or the address space offers no partial check or filesystem block size covers the folio. Otherwise it trims the requested byte range to the folio span and delegates the remainder test to the address space operation, excluding whole folio reads from the partial path.

Single folio read tracks working set membership for stall accounting around the filesystem filler, waits killably for the folio lock after submission, reports success only when the folio becomes current, and on transfer failure shrinks the file readahead window to a quarter.

Creation for reads rejects nonblocking and queued modes, allocates a minimal order folio with the mapping reclaim mask, applies a dropbehind hint when requested, computes an aligned index from file position, inserts under shared invalidation protection, translates concurrent existence into a truncated retry signal, reads content through the filesystem operation, and on any error releases protection and reference.

Readahead growth is geometric with tiny windows growing fastest and larger windows capped at maximum, while initial size rounds the request up to a power of two then scales by thresholds relative to maximum. The async path additionally increases order, derives an alignment power from order and maximum, and trims the window end down to that alignment.

Ordered allocation creates a folio at a chosen order, rounds the marker down to the folio span and flags the folio when indices coincide, inserts into the cache, accounts page count and working set contribution, and on insertion failure releases the folio and stops further allocation.
Maximum readahead pages default to the file readahead limit but may expand up to the device optimal input output size when the request exceeds the limit and the device optimum is larger.

Hot marking is suppressed for folios already marked or not current or flagged for readahead or dropbehind or unevictable, otherwise it sets the marker once and accounts the folio span. Position comparison judges two byte offsets as sharing a folio when they agree after shifting by the folio shift.

Cache scans and miss probes hold read side protection across tree traversal and reference acquisition, releasing before return. Async and sync paths use the same protection only around miss queries, not across window mutation or submission.

When locking is requested, nonblocking mode attempts a try lock and reports retryable contention after dropping the reference, while blocking mode waits. After acquiring, the mapping is revalidated and truncated folios are unlocked, released, and cause a fresh lookup. Stability waits occur only after lock handling and access marking.

Read, creation, and ordered readahead paths hold shared invalidation protection while checking currency, inserting new folios, mapping blocks, or submitting reads, preventing instantiation races with truncation and hole punch. Nonblocking reads use a try variant that reports retryable on contention. Ordered readahead additionally suppresses filesystem reclaim around the protected region and always releases both guards.

Read update first attempts a nonblocking folio lock, with nonblocking and no input output and queued modes failing immediately as retryable on contention. Without queueing it drops invalidation protection and waits killably before signalling truncation retry, while with queueing it registers an async waiter.

Read update progresses through invalidation acquisition, folio lock acquisition, truncation check on missing mapping, currency check, and either success unlock or filler submission. Truncation releases the folio reference and signals retry, restricted modes short circuit filler submission as retryable, and filler errors propagate after releasing invalidation protection.

Buffered preparation cycles among batch collection, synchronous readahead, folio creation, async trigger on marked tail, and currency enforcement. Empty batches drive the next stage, multi folio batches with a non current tail short circuit as retryable, single folio non current tails go through update, and truncated signals restart the cycle.

Observed address space state exposes a page tree with an owning host and an operation table, folio state exposes an owning mapping with an index plus flags for currency and readahead and dropbehind and idle and dirty and writeback and working set and evictability, and batches expose a count with an array plus add and count helpers and caller maintained start cursors.

Observed readahead state carries a page limit with a window start and size and async portion and order and previous position, control state carries a mapping with readahead state and file and current index and page count and working set flag and dropbehind request, input output control carries a file pointer with position and flags and wait queue, and file state carries a mapping with readahead state and mode.

Callers must treat retryable, truncated, interrupt, and transfer outcomes as control signals rather than fatal errors. Contention and nonblocking allocation use retryable, concurrent insertion and truncation restart lookup or preparation, fatal signals abort preparation, and failed reads after submission surface as transfer errors while shrinking future readahead.

Caching hints have side effects. Creation may pre mark dropbehind to favour early reclaim, while ordinary lookup clears a stale dropbehind marker and, when the folio is dirty on a writeback capable mapping, decrements a writeback dirty counter by the folio span under writeback guards. Missing lock or mmap flags on creation are repaired by forcing locking with a one time warning.

Contract distinguishes retryable contention from allocation failure and missing entry, with concurrent insertion and transfer failure and signal interruption and truncation retry as further distinct outcomes. Numeric encodings are not visible in these fragments.

Lookup and read control use separate symbolic bits for locking and nonblocking operation alongside companions for creation and access marking and write intent and stability and cacheability and mmap handling, while read control uses further bits for nowait and no input output and wait queue and dontcache with a random mode selector. Bit positions are not visible.
